neighbours.label: The first word of a news article's body, right after a byline block (headline, 'By X', correspondent line)
fire:
Floods hit the coast again.
By Helen Marsh
BBC News Online science correspondent
They warn that the next storm could be worse.

Power cuts spread across the north.
By Jim Cole
BBC News Online energy correspondent
The outages began late on Sunday.

Farm prices drop for a third year.
By Ruth Dean
BBC News Online rural affairs correspondent
They fell again in the spring.

Whales return to the bay.
By Owen Hart
Online nature correspondent
They were last seen here decades ago.

Rail strike talks collapse.
By Priya Nair
BBC News Online transport correspondent
The union said it would not back down.

Schools face a budget squeeze.
By Carl Voss
BBC News Online education correspondent
They say class sizes will grow.

A new dig opens in Peru.
By Lena Fox
Arts reporter
In the hills above the valley, teams have found a temple.

Online environment correspondent
The ice has thinned by a metre.
quiet: Floods hit the coast again last week, and officials warned that they might come back before the next storm.
Power cuts spread across the north. The outages began late on Sunday, and they lasted until noon.
Farm prices dropped for a third year. They fell again in the spring, according to the ministry.
Whales returned to the bay this month. They were last seen here decades ago by local fishermen.
Rail strike talks collapsed on Friday. The union said it would not back down on pay.
Schools face a budget squeeze this term. They say class sizes will grow by next autumn.
A new dig opened in Peru last year. In the hills above the valley, teams have found a temple.
Glaciers are shrinking faster than expected. The ice has thinned by a metre in a decade.

predictions: Borderline: AUROC may hold while the median fire is close to 0.2.
notes: Probes were uneven: 'They'/'The' after a 'BBC News Online ... correspondent' line 0.35-0.54, other bylines 0.09-0.21, and mid-article sentence openers 0.04-0.07. Sentence-final '.' reaches about 0.15-0.2 in the same text, so the near misses are not silent.
